hub_card_summary_html: Live cohort Socratic discussion & 5 explainer clips accompanying Legal Engineering 101 Class 7.2 on collapsible nested if/else clause trees, Hats Protocol contract chaining, the Leibniz–Goldfarb–Szabo–Grigg computational lineage, Russell/Gödel/Church formal logic limits, and REPSL osFig infrastructure.
overview_html: In this live cohort Socratic session for Lesson 7.2: Translating Clauses into Nested If/Else Logic, participants explore how traditional indented legal clauses and subclauses map directly into collapsible nested if/else conditional trees and Hats Protocol modular contract dependencies, why LexClinic combines a Free/Libre Open Source Software (FLOSS / AGPL-3.0) educational base with a non-commercial patent license for US Patent 12,664,142 (SeedTree), how legal minds laid the foundations of modern computing—from Robert Recorde's 1557 = sign and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz's 1666 De Arte Combinatoria (Doctor of Law) to Harvard JD Charles Goldfarb's GML/SGML (<!DOCTYPE html>), Nick Szabo's Smart Contracts, and Ian Grigg's Ricardian Contracts—why Bertrand Russell's 1901 Barber Paradox, Kurt Gödel's 1931 Incompleteness Theorems, and Alonzo Church's 1936 λ-calculus prove that self-referential legal systems require sovereign human exception handlers, and how REPSL osFig (🔱) VMs and local F5-TTS voice synthesis power the platform.

takeaways.heading_html: ⚖️ Collapsible Nested If/Else Trees & Hats Protocol Chaining
takeaways.body_html: Translating indented prose clauses and subclauses into falling-domino nested if/else hierarchies (distinguishing right-to-left = state assignment from == equality evaluation) and chaining standalone modular contracts via Hats Protocol trees.

takeaways.heading_html: 🏛️ How Lawyers Built Computing (Leibniz, Goldfarb, Szabo & Grigg)
takeaways.body_html: Tracing computational law from Robert Recorde (1557 = sign) and jurist Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (characteristica universalis & calculus ratiocinator) to attorney Charles Goldfarb (GML/SGML/HTML), Nick Szabo (Smart Contracts), and Ian Grigg (Ricardian Contracts).

takeaways.heading_html: 🧮 The Mathematical Limits of Logic (Russell, Gödel & Church)
takeaways.body_html: Why Bertrand Russell's 1901 Barber Paradox, Kurt Gödel's 1931 Incompleteness Theorems (Gödel numbering), and Alonzo Church's 1936 λ-calculus (Entscheidungsproblem) prove that formal code cannot be both complete and consistent without human fiduciary adjudication.

takeaways.heading_html: ☁️ Dual FLOSS/SeedTree Licensing & REPSL osFig Infrastructure
takeaways.body_html: Combining AGPL-3.0 open-source education with non-commercial licensing of US Patent 12,664,142 (SeedTree), zero-config REPSL osFig (🔱) VMs on Google Cloud, the 4-pillar brand architecture (ICE, CPU, FAK, MRI), and local F5-TTS voice cloning.
